item.title: Emmy Awards winners list for 2026: Live updates
item.description: The 78th Primetime Emmy Awards are celebrating the best in television and streaming. See the full list of winners and nominees.

item.title: Supreme Court rejects Trump mail ballot restrictions for now
item.description: The Supreme Court on Monday blocked the Postal Service's new rules for mail ballots while a legal challenge plays out, in a blow to President Trump's agenda. CBS News legal contributor Jessica Levinson breaks down the ruling.

item.title: What could a global pause on AI look like?
item.description: Several top tech CEOs are calling for a slowdown in artificial intelligence development amid industry concerns that the technology is spiraling out of control. In a recent New York Times opinion piece, investigative journalist Stephen Witt argues that slowing down may not be enough. Witt joins CBS News to explain.

item.title: 70-year-old hiker found after he was missing for a week
item.description: A 70-year-old hiker, lost for a week on a large island in the middle of Lake Superior, has been found, after search and rescue teams had nearly given up hope. Mark Strassmann has the story.

item.title: Torrential rains slam Connecticut, triggering dangerous flash floods
item.description: In parts of the Northeast, Sunday was one of the rainiest days in years, and on Monday, more dangerous storms rolled through the Central U.S. Tornado watches are also posted in Iowa. Lana Zak reports, and Andrew Kozak has the forecast.

item.title: Video captures young girl getting run over by truck, miraculously surviving
item.description: Surveillance video captured a young girl with her backpack and phone in hand crossing a busy street in Philadelphia. Moments later, a truck appeared to run her over, dragging her under its wheels. Miraculously, she was able to walk away. Cristian Benavides has the story.

item.title: Mitch McConnell seen publicly for first time since June
item.description: Republican Sen. Mitch McConnell of Kentucky was seen in Washington, D.C., on Monday, for the first time since June. Ed O'Keefe reports.

item.title: Supreme Court blocks new Postal Service rules for mail ballots in blow to Trump
item.description: The Supreme Court left intact a ruling that blocked the U.S. Postal Service from enforcing new regulations for mail voting, rejecting the Trump administration's effort to move forward with the rules in the midterms.

item.title: Don Jr.'s wife says Russian oligarch hosted post-wedding festivities as a "gift"
item.description: Bettina Anderson, wife of Donald Trump Jr., said their "dear friend" Umar Kremlev hosted two nights of festivities after their wedding in the Bahamas.

item.title: As gas averages $4.31 nationwide, diesel fuel hits all-time high: "It's painful. It's real hard"
item.description: Gas prices are running about 15 cents per gallon more than they were just a week ago, and diesel fuel for trucks is now at an all-time high, topping $6 a gallon. The war with Iran is the biggest factor, but President Trump is instead blaming Ukraine. Ed O'Keefe has more details.

item.title: Top Trump AI adviser says if China wins AI race, U.S. "will not be the number one country" anymore
item.description: Over the weekend, four of America's top tech leaders, including Elon Musk, agreed that AI's development should slow down and called for government standards. President Trump dismissed their calls, and in a CBS News exclusive, one of the president's top AI advisers, David Sacks, reacted. Jo Ling Kent reports.

item.title: Pennsylvania woman dies of measles complications, coroner reports
item.description: A 40-year-old woman died on Saturday from complications associated with measles, the coroner reported.

item.title: Looking back at Bob Mackie's signature looks, life after his death at 87
item.description: Bob Mackie, a fashion icon known for elevating Hollywood's leading ladies and pop stars for decades, died on Monday at 87. Meg Oliver looks back on his signature looks and his life.

item.title: Sen. Mitch McConnell returns to Congress after 3-month absence
item.description: Republican Sen. Mitch McConnell of Kentucky returned to Capitol Hill on Monday after a monthslong absence. CBS News congressional reporter Taurean Small has the latest.

item.title: Lower-paid workers who change jobs seeing biggest pay raises in more than 3 years, report finds
item.description: One group of American workers is seeing their fastest wage growth in more than three years as they jump ship and change jobs. CBS News MoneyWatch reporter Megan Cerullo explains.

item.title: Blanche claims evidence for mail-in voting fraud is "common sense"
item.description: In an interview with CBS News' Nicole Sganga, Attorney General Todd Blanche claimed mail-in voting carried a greater risk of fraud than in-person voting with ID. When asked what evidence he had to support his statement, he responded, "Well, it's common sense."

item.title: Alligator Alcatraz had cramped conditions, "small metal enclosures," watchdog finds
item.description: DHS's internal watchdog is sharply criticizing conditions in a Florida immigration detention center dubbed "Alligator Alcatraz," finding detainees at the now-closed facility were held in "cramped conditions."

item.title: Senate returns for final legislative sprint ahead of midterms
item.description: The Senate returned to Washington from a five-week recess, with several priorities to address before leaving town next month to take to the campaign trail.

item.title: Tech stocks slump after AI execs call for industry slowdown
item.description: The tech-heavy Nasdaq slumped 147 points on Monday after AI company executives called for a slowdown in developing the technology.

item.title: Blanche vows to release more 9/11 docs: "We're not protecting people"
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche says the government is not withholding documents to protect another country, days after 9/11 families publicly appealed to the Trump administration for more information to be released.

item.title: Blanche says more 9/11 documents will be released
item.description: Attorney General Todd Blanche told CBS News' Nicole Sganga that the federal government will continue releasing records related to the Sept. 11, 2001, terror attacks. "The one thing that we are not doing, we're not protecting people," Blanche said. "The reason that we're not releasing documents has nothing to do with protecting any government or any entity. It's just to protect, genuine classified information."

item.title: AI companies must ensure their tech is safe, says top Trump adviser on AI
item.description: In an interview with CBS News, Sacks suggested that fears AI could harm people are overblown. "I think this is becoming a panic," he said.

item.title: Lane Kiffin set to make highly anticipated Ole Miss return
item.description: This Saturday will be far from a welcome homecoming for college football's most polarizing coach, LSU's Lane Kiffin. Kiffin will be facing his old team, the University of Mississippi, and his departure from Ole Miss in the middle of last season was anything but amicable. CBS Sports' John Talty, author of the forthcoming book "Lane Being Lane," joins "The Takeout" to discuss.

item.title: John Brennan subpoenaed in Florida "grand conspiracy" probe
item.description: Former CIA Director John Brennan was subpoenaed to testify before a grand jury in Florida as part of the "grand conspiracy" investigation into Obama- and Biden-era officials last week.

item.title: Mitch McConnell returns to Capitol Hill after monthslong absence
item.description: GOP Sen. Mitch McConnell of Kentucky returned to Capitol Hill on Monday for the first time in three months, ending a prolonged absence that sparked widespread speculation about his health.

item.title: Iconic designer Bob Mackie dies at 87. See photos of legendary stars he dressed.
item.description: Dubbed the "Designer to the Stars," Bob Mackie won nine Emmy Awards, a Tony Award and was nominated for three Oscars.

item.title: Trump dismisses push for AI guardrails despite warnings from tech leaders
item.description: President Trump threw cold water on momentum for AI guardrails, saying all the U.S. needs is a "SMART (High IQ!) PRESIDENT."

item.title: 9/14: The Takeout with Major Garrett
item.description: Anthropic CEO joins growing calls for AI slowdown; President Trump demands Ukraine stop targeting Russian oil refineries.

item.title: Oil prices stay above $100 as Iran and Oman delay Strait of Hormuz talks
item.description: Iran and Oman delayed a meeting to discuss control of the Strait of Hormuz as fighting between Iran's Houthi allies and Saudi Arabia raises the stakes for global energy markets.

item.title: Vance says 870K people suspected of COVID-era U.S. fraud barred from federal loans
item.description: A U.S. enforcement push, dubbed "Heartland fraud surge," probed losses involving the Paycheck Protection Program and Economic Injury Disaster Loan program.
